ENGLISH — TERMLY EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

2. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. blue

4. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

5. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)

6. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Handwriting: Legibility and Neatness.

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. Only one word repeated

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive reading: Simple poems.

9. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goes

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a joining word

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

13. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)

15. When practising Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation Marks.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Independent Reading: Visuals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 7.3.1: Personal and possessive pronouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
